name: Business Current Account Opening
description: An SME or corporate customer applies for and opens a business current account. The journey encompasses Know Your Business (KYB) checks via Companies House API, Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) identification and verification under MLR 2017 Regulation 5 (natural persons with >25% ownership or control), individual identity verification for each director and UBO, company-level and individual-level CDD/EDD assessment, automated account decisioning, multi-signatory account provisioning on the Commercial Banking Core, and business digital channel activation. Establishes the BusinessCustomer and BusinessAccount aggregate roots consumed by all downstream commercial journeys (JRN-007, JRN-013, JRN-014, JRN-023). Mandated by the bank's PRA deposit-taking permission, MLR 2017 Regulation 28 (enhanced CDD for legal entities with complex ownership), and FCA BCA switching obligations.

happy_path_sla.description: Standard business current account opening (limited company, standard CDD, no EDD required)
happy_path_sla.notes: Longer than JRN-001 (personal, <10 minutes automated) due to UBO identification and individual identity verification for each director/UBO. Companies House API lookup and Encompass KYB report generation add asynchronous processing time. Target: same-day Companies House verification; 1-2 business days for director/UBO identity verification; 1-2 business days for CDD assessment completion.

edd_path_sla.description: Enhanced Due Diligence path (PEP director, high-risk jurisdiction company, complex ownership structure)
edd_path_sla.notes: MLRO review required. EDD evidence gathering (source of funds, source of wealth for each UBO, enhanced adverse media monitoring) adds processing time. PER-050 (Relationship Manager) assists the customer in gathering required documentation.

phases.name: Application Initiation
phases.description: The business applicant (PER-002) initiates account opening via the web portal (CH-001) or mobile app (CH-002). Business registration details are collected: legal entity type, company name, Companies House registration number, registered address, trading address (if different), trading name (if applicable), SIC codes, and incorporation date. The applicant selects the account type (standard business current account, multi-currency account). A preliminary eligibility check confirms the entity type is supported (limited company, LLP, partnership, sole trader — each has a different subsequent path). BusinessApplicationStarted domain event is published and a provisional application reference is assigned.
phases.governance_notes: MLR 2017 Regulation 28 requires enhanced CDD for legal persons before establishing a business relationship. BBRS disclosure (GOV-002-R03) must be made available to eligible SME customers at account opening. Consumer Duty principles apply to business customers within scope of FCA oversight. SCA not required at pre-authentication initiation stage.
entry_conditions: Applicant has accessed web portal (CH-001) or mobile app (CH-002)
Applicant confirms they are an authorised signatory or officer of the business
Entity type selected: limited company | LLP | partnership | sole trader
No pre-existing active business account detected for the same Companies House number (deduplication check)
exit_conditions: Business registration details submitted
Preliminary eligibility check passed
BusinessApplicationStarted event published with application_ref assigned
Customer progresses to Companies House verification (BPH-002)
exit_conditions_failure: Dormant company detected — exception path EX-B001 (dormant company review)

Applicant cannot confirm authorisation — referral to PER-050 Relationship Manager

alt_paths.name: Sole Trader
alt_paths.description: Sole trader path: Companies House lookup not applicable. Identity verification for the individual only (no UBO identification required — sole trader is the single beneficial owner). CDD follows the simplified business path. Estimated SLA: 1-2 business days.

alt_paths.name: Partnership
alt_paths.description: Partnership path: no Companies House number. Partner identification replaces director/UBO identification — all partners must be identified and verified. Risk typically elevated due to less transparent structure.

alt_paths.name: LLP
alt_paths.description: Limited Liability Partnership path: Companies House number required. Designated members treated as directors. Members with >25% profit share treated as UBOs. LLP agreement required as supporting document.

phases.name: Companies House Verification
phases.description: SVC-005 (Commercial Banking Core) calls the Companies House API to retrieve and validate the company record. The lookup returns: registered company name, company number, company status (active/dissolved/dormant), company type, registered address, incorporation date, SIC codes, current appointed directors (officer list), and Persons with Significant Control (PSC) filings — which constitute the starting point for UBO identification. The API response is reconciled against the applicant-provided data. Any discrepancies (name mismatch, dormant status, mismatched address) trigger exception handling. CompaniesHouseVerified event is published on successful validation.
phases.governance_notes: MLR 2017 Regulation 28(11) requires the bank to obtain and verify company registration information from a reliable and independent source — the Companies House public register satisfies this requirement. PSC filings under the Companies Act 2006 (as amended by the Small Business, Enterprise and Employment Act 2015) are the primary source for initial UBO identification. PSC data must be cross-checked and not solely relied upon — nominees and complex structures require additional investigation.

Companies House registration number provided by applicant
Entity type = limited company or LLP
exit_conditions: Companies House API returns company status = active
Registered company name and address reconciled with applicant-provided data
Director list and PSC list extracted and stored in DirectorRecord and initial UBO staging
CompaniesHouseVerified event published

phases.name: Director and UBO Identification
phases.description: SVC-005 constructs the complete ownership and control structure of the entity using the Companies House PSC data and director list retrieved in BPH-002. MLR 2017 Regulation 5 defines beneficial owner for a body corporate as any natural person who: (a) holds, directly or indirectly, more than 25% of shares; (b) holds, directly or indirectly, more than 25% of voting rights; or (c) holds the right to appoint or remove a majority of directors. All such natural persons must be identified as UBOs. Additionally, all current appointed directors must be identified as DirectorRecords regardless of ownership percentage (they may be PEPs or sanctions matches). Where the PSC is itself a legal entity (corporate UBO), the bank must 'look through' to identify the natural persons behind that entity. The applicant is prompted to confirm the UBO list, declare any additional beneficial owners not listed in Companies House filings, and provide details for each UBO. UBOIdentified events are published for each confirmed UBO.
phases.governance_notes: MLR 2017 Regulation 5 (definition of beneficial owner for legal persons). Regulation 28(3)(a) requires identifying and taking reasonable measures to verify the identity of beneficial owners. JMLSG Part II guidance on corporate structures requires penetrating holding company layers. If no natural person can be identified as beneficial owner (e.g. widely-held listed company), the senior managing official(s) must be treated as the beneficial owner of last resort under Regulation 5(4). The bank must document its UBO identification methodology and keep records of any cases where a natural person cannot be identified (MLR 2017 Regulation 40).

Director list and PSC data available in SVC-005
exit_conditions: All directors identified and DirectorRecord entities created

phases.name: Identity Verification
phases.description: Each identified director and UBO must undergo individual identity verification via SVC-050 (Customer Onboarding Service). The primary applicant (PER-002) completes identity verification during the online journey. Each additional director and UBO receives a secure digital invitation link to complete their identity verification independently (document capture + biometric liveness check via Onfido/Jumio). Address verification is required for each individual. The system tracks verification status per individual — account processing cannot proceed until all required verifications are complete. Where a director or UBO is already a verified personal customer of the bank, a match against existing IdentityVerification records may satisfy the requirement (with MLRO approval). DirectorVerified events are published for each successful verification. All individual verifications must be complete before BPH-005.
phases.governance_notes: MLR 2017 Regulation 28(3) requires verifying the identity of directors and beneficial owners. Each individual verification must meet the same standard as personal customer CDD — document authentication, biometric liveness check, address verification. UK GDPR Article 9 applies to biometric data — DPIA covers this extension of the eKYC pipeline to business customer UBOs. Verification status must be traceable per individual in the audit trail to satisfy MLR 2017 Regulation 40 record-keeping obligations.

phases.name: KYC/CDD Assessment
phases.description: SVC-014 (KYC/AML Service) performs a two-tier CDD assessment: (1) Company-level CDD — PEP/sanctions screening on the company name and registration number, adverse media screening on the company, sector risk assessment (SIC code risk scoring), jurisdictional risk (country of incorporation, trading countries), and company status review. (2) Individual-level CDD — PEP/sanctions/adverse media screening for each verified director and UBO individually. A BusinessKycAssessment entity is created for the company, referencing individual director and UBO assessment results. Risk scoring incorporates: company structure complexity, UBO jurisdiction risk, director PEP status, sector risk, adverse media findings, and source of business funds. EDD is triggered if: any director or UBO is a PEP; the company is incorporated in or operates in a high-risk jurisdiction (FATF list, HM Treasury designated countries); the company structure is complex with multiple holding layers; or the company risk score exceeds the EDD threshold. BusinessKYCCleared event is published on successful standard CDD completion.
phases.governance_notes: MLR 2017 Regulation 33 requires EDD for high-risk third countries, PEPs, and complex corporate structures. MLR 2017 Regulation 28(11) requires verifying the nature and purpose of the business relationship. JMLSG Part II Guidance on Corporate and Institutional Customers applies. OFSI Consolidated List and OFAC screening must cover the company, all directors, and all UBOs (GOV-005-R02). Sanctions screening must traverse the full UBO ownership chain — not just name-matching at the top entity level. pKYC monitoring must be initiated for the company entity on account opening (GOV-005-R06).

CompaniesHouseVerified event received
All UBO identity verifications complete with outcome = pass

phases.name: Account Decision
phases.description: SVC-005 (Commercial Banking Core) receives the BusinessKYCCleared event and runs the automated business account decision engine. Decision inputs: Companies House verification outcome, all UBO identity verification outcomes, BusinessKycAssessment risk_category, sector risk, company age (incorporation_date), company status. Decision outcomes: Approved (standard CDD, all checks passed), Referred (manual RM review — borderline risk, complex structure), Declined (risk exceeds threshold, unresolvable ownership ambiguity, sanctions-adjacent concerns). BusinessApplicationDecisionMade event is published with the decision outcome. Approved applications immediately trigger BPH-007 Account Provisioning. PER-050 (Relationship Manager) is notified of referred applications and must resolve within 5 business days.
phases.governance_notes: BBRS complaint referral signpost (GOV-002-R03) must be included in decline communications for eligible SME customers. Automated decision evidence must be retained as the Consumer Duty (and incoming SME lending rules GOV-002-R05) fair value record. Declined applications must include an internal reason code; the customer receives a plain-language decline message without disclosure of specific CDD findings (tipping-off principle applied by analogy).

exit_conditions: BusinessApplicationDecisionMade event published

phases.name: Account Provisioning
phases.description: SVC-005 (Commercial Banking Core) creates the BusinessAccount entity. Business account number and sort code are allocated from the bank's commercial banking range. Multi-signatory configuration is applied based on the authorised signatories declared by PER-002 during application. Payment approval workflow rules are configured: single-authoriser vs dual-authorisation for payments above a configurable threshold. BACS, Faster Payments, and CHAPS access are enabled. The BusinessCustomer aggregate root is promoted from 'prospect' to 'active'. FSCS eligibility is assessed (business accounts are eligible if the business meets FSCS eligible depositor criteria — sole traders and small partnerships only; limited companies generally not eligible). BusinessAccountOpened and BusinessAccountProvisioned events are published. Companies House data is cross-referenced to the BusinessCustomer entity.
phases.governance_notes: CASS business account switching obligations (GOV-002-R06) require CASS registration within the applicable switching window once the regime is extended to business accounts. FSCS eligibility determination for business accounts: sole traders are eligible depositors; limited companies are not. This must be determined at provisioning and reflected in the FSCS SCV if applicable. BusinessAccountProvisioned event must carry the multi-signatory configuration for SVC-017 to set up the business portal with correct user roles.

BusinessCustomer entity exists with status = prospect

phases.name: Digital Channel Activation
phases.description: SVC-017 (Digital Channels) enrolls the business customer in the business online banking portal. The primary applicant (PER-002) sets up their personal credentials and biometric SCA (FIDO2/WebAuthn) for the business portal. Each additional authorised user declared in multi-signatory configuration receives a secure portal invitation. User roles are provisioned according to the authorised_users configuration on BusinessAccount (e.g. sole payment authoriser, payment initiator only, view-only finance controller). The business portal displays: account number, sort code, IBAN, BIC, multi-signatory payment workflow configuration, and a welcome onboarding checklist. BusinessDigitalChannelActivated event is published on completion.
phases.governance_notes: PSR 2017 Regulation 100 SCA compliance: business portal access must be gated by SCA-compliant authentication for each authorised user. Multi-user business portal access must enforce role-based access controls — a payment initiator cannot also be the approver of the same payment (separation of duties). UK GDPR data minimisation: each authorised user has their own credential — no shared usernames.

BusinessAccount.status = active
exit_conditions: PER-002 primary user has completed credential setup and biometric SCA enrolment
All authorised users have portal invitations dispatched

exception_paths.name: Dormant Company
exception_paths.description: Companies House returns company status = dormant. Application cannot proceed automatically. Referred to PER-050 (Relationship Manager) who contacts PER-002 for explanation of intended trading activity. If satisfactory: manual override by RM; application proceeds. If unsatisfactory: application declined. SLA: RM response within 2 business days.

exception_paths.name: Dissolved or Struck-Off Company
exception_paths.description: Companies House returns company status = dissolved, liquidation, or administration. Application is immediately declined. PER-002 receives notification that the bank is unable to open an account for the entity in its current status. Referral to BBRS signpost included for eligible SMEs.

exception_paths.name: Companies House Data Mismatch
exception_paths.description: Applicant-provided company name or registered address does not reconcile with Companies House data beyond allowable variation threshold. PER-002 is prompted to correct the data or provide supporting documentation. If unresolvable digitally, PER-050 RM assists manually.

exception_paths.name: UBO Not Identifiable
exception_paths.description: The corporate structure does not permit identification of natural persons behind the 25% threshold (e.g. complex multi-layer offshore holding structure). Referred immediately to MLRO (PER-052) for enhanced UBO investigation. PER-050 RM coordinates document gathering. If UBO cannot be identified to the MLRO's satisfaction, the application is declined under MLR 2017 Regulation 21(3).

exception_paths.name: Fraud Detected on Director/UBO Document
exception_paths.description: Identity verification vendor returns outcome = fraud_detected for a director or UBO. Application suspended immediately. MLRO (PER-052) notified. A Suspicious Activity Report (SAR) may be required under POCA 2002 s330. Customer receives standard failure message — tipping-off prohibition applies. Application is blocked.

exception_paths.name: Sanctions Hit on Company, Director, or UBO
exception_paths.description: SVC-051 returns sanctions match against the company name, a director, or a UBO against OFSI/OFAC/UN/EU Consolidated Lists. BusinessSanctionsHitDetected event published. Application immediately blocked. MLRO (PER-052) must review within 1 business day and report to OFSI within 14 days if confirmed designation (GOV-005-R02). No information disclosed to PER-002 regarding the sanctions match — standard decline message only (tipping-off prohibition POCA 2002 s333A).

exception_paths.name: Account Provisioning Failure
exception_paths.description: Technical failure in business account number/sort code allocation or BusinessCustomer promotion. IT Operations (PER-060) alerted via SVC-103. Automatic retry with idempotency guarantee (max 3 retries over 15 minutes). If all retries fail, manual provisioning by PER-060 with incident ticket. PER-002 informed of delay with updated SLA.

alternative_paths.name: Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) Review
alternative_paths.description: Triggered when: (1) any director or UBO is identified as a PEP; (2) company operates in or is incorporated in a high-risk jurisdiction (FATF grey/black list or HM Treasury designated high-risk third country); (3) complex corporate ownership structure requiring look-through; (4) company risk score exceeds EDD threshold. PER-052 (MLRO) is assigned the case. PER-050 (Relationship Manager) contacts PER-002 to gather EDD evidence: source of business funds, source of UBO wealth, corporate ownership chart, board resolution confirming authorised signatories. MLRO must sign off the EDD assessment before the application proceeds to BPH-006. SLA: 10 business days for EDD completion.

alternative_paths.name: Relationship Manager Assisted Application
alternative_paths.description: For complex corporate structures, large corporate customers (>£10m annual turnover), or customers with PEP directors, PER-050 (Relationship Manager) may assist PER-002 in completing the application. The RM can initiate and pre-populate the application in the commercial banking CRM, view real-time application status, and coordinate document collection on behalf of the customer. The RM cannot override CDD/KYC outcomes — only MLRO (PER-052) can.

primary_regulations: MLR 2017 Regulation 28 — enhanced CDD for legal persons (company verification, UBO identification)
MLR 2017 Regulation 5 — definition of beneficial owner for body corporate (>25% threshold)
MLR 2017 Regulation 33 — enhanced due diligence for high-risk scenarios
MLR 2017 Regulation 40 — record-keeping obligations (5 years post-relationship end)
OFSI Consolidated List screening — GOV-005-R02 (real-time, covers all UBOs and directors)
GOV-002-R03 — BBRS disclosure to eligible SME customers at account opening
Companies Act 2006 (as amended) — PSC register requirements
FCA BCA switching — GOV-002-R06 (incoming CASS business account portability)
key_compliance_dependencies: Companies House API must be available and returning current data
SVC-051 Sanctions Screening must be capable of screening the full UBO ownership chain (not just top-level entity name)
SVC-050 Customer Onboarding must support multiple concurrent individual identity verifications per application
MLRO (PER-052) case management workflow must be in place for EDD referrals
